intro: Every setting below is written into autounattend.xml when you build the file. Nothing here is read from this PC, so the tables show the answer-file pass, component and path each value lands in instead of a registry key.

groups.Processor architecture: Which processor architectures the file covers. Every component in the file is written once per architecture you tick, so one file can install on x64, ARM64 and x86 PCs.
groups.Edition and product key: The edition Setup installs, and the key it uses to pick it. The built-in keys select an edition without activating Windows; your own key selects and activates.
groups.Windows 11 requirements: Setup's checks for TPM 2.0, Secure Boot and the RAM, storage, CPU and disk minimums. Turning them off lets Setup install on a PC that fails them.
groups.Accounts: How the first account is created, and the local accounts Setup makes before the first sign-in. In Winhance each account you add also carries a display name, a group, a password and the sign-in options; the part that is the same on every PC, and so the part documented here, is the name rule below.
groups.Setup screens: The pages Setup shows while Windows installs, and the name this PC gets on the network. Turning a page off answers it in the file so Setup does not stop there.
groups.General: What Setup adds once Windows is installed: .NET Framework 3.5 from the installation media, and an Install Winhance shortcut on the desktop of every new account.
